newsitem.title: UK: RTZ-CRA shares rebound after H1 results.
newsitem.headline: RTZ-CRA shares rebound after H1 results.

text.p: Shares in mining giant RTZ-CRA bounced higher on Thursday, recovering from an early tumble as hopes for a recovery in metal prices outweighed profits at the low end of expectations, traders said.
The stock recovered to stand 34p up at 964-1/2p by 0807 GMT, after tumbling initially to 918p. Analysts comments from RTZ suggested potential for a future recovery in metal prices.
"Sir Derek Birkin's statement talks about metal prices being more depressed than fundamentals would indicate," said Charles Kernot, mining analyst at Paribas Capital Markets.
"That could mean things could move higher over the next couple of years as prices go up with economic growth."

RTZ, the world's biggest mining company, said net adjusted earnings fell to $552 million in the first half of 1996, from $711 million a year before. Analysts forecasts were in a range of $516 million to $558 million.
The company said earnings had been hit by lower metal prices, exchange rate movements and delays to a new U.S. copper smelter.
RTZ chairman Sir Derek Birkin said: "The current price levels of many metals appear to be more depressed than the fundamentals of supply, demand and stocks would suggest."
Analysts said results from the company's diamond exploration programme in Canada also added shine to the results. "I think the results look very interesting," said Kernot.
RTZ said results from Canada were promising with initial valuations of samples processed so far comparing favourably with operating mines around the world.

Robert Wilson, chief executive of RTZ-CRA, said exploration results generally were promising, with greater efficiencies following a refocusing and restructuring of global exploration expected to show savings of $50 million per year from 1997.
